reproduction_target: OpenMM coarse-grained bead-spring polymer simulation of human chromosome 1 (50,000 beads, 5 kb/bead, r0=30 nm) under a three-layer loop-extrusion model (Condensin I/II nested loops + megabase super-loops). Reproduce: collapse of a 25 um bottle-brush into a 5-8 x 1.5 um rod, the second-diagonal peak in mitotic Hi-C contact maps, and the double-helical scaffold, across 55 looping conformations (25 consecutive, 25 interlaced, 5 multi-laced) plus super-loop-size sweeps (3/5/7/12/15 Mb).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-computational-stage from Methods prose. Only one external named tool (OpenMM, cited as 'OpenMM 8'); remaining stages run in-house Python (Simulator_Chromatin.py, Pars.py). Repo landing/README read at prose level only (stage-1); no workflow source read line-by-line. No wet-lab: experimental validation is proposed future work, not performed (W=0).

steps.label: Looping-conformation initialization (Pars.py): Gaussian sampling of Condensin II loops (mean 480 kb, sigma 30 kb, 50 kb gaps), nested Condensin I loops (mean 90 kb, sigma 10 kb), and super-loops (mean 9.7 Mb, sigma 0.4 Mb); 55 conformations across consecutive/interlaced/multi-laced regimes

OpenMM coarse-grained polymer MD simulation (Simulator_Chromatin.py) on CUDA: harmonic bonds/angles, NonbondedForce (sigma_vdW=28 nm), CustomBondForce (k=25/50/80 kJ/mol/nm2), VariableLangevinIntegrator (300 K, friction 0.003 ps^-1, tol 0.003), energy minimization then 5e5-step blocks with staged epsilon_vdW (0.1 -> 0.3)

Structural / contact-map analysis and figure generation: simulated Hi-C contact-frequency profiles (second-diagonal comparison), rod dimensions, double-helical scaffold and alternating-handedness/zero-mean helicity readouts, compared against published mitotic Hi-C [ref 4] and 3D-SIM imaging

headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on all 3 computational steps. R★ not assignable at stage1. Environment is floating: repo README states only 'The code is compatible with OpenMM 8' (major version, no exact patch/CUDA/Python pin), and the repo carries no environment.yml, lockfile, or container. Because the capture claim is 'floating' (not exact_pins/release_snapshot/env_lock/container), this paper is NOT a stage2 R★ candidate: even a perfect stage2 run could not exceed RI without a pinned/lockable environment. C3 additionally lacks in-repo analysis/plotting code and depends on reference Hi-C data available only via citation.
headline.coverage: 3 computational steps assessed from Methods prose + repo landing/README (2 Python scripts + coords/ input files). No wet-lab steps (W=0); proposed experimental validation is future work.

gaps.where: Software environment (repo README + Methods): OpenMM used for all forces/integration
gaps.missing: No environment.yml / lockfile / container. README pins only 'OpenMM 8' (major version); OpenMM patch version, CUDA toolkit/driver version, Python version, and any helper libraries are unspecified. Simulations are CUDA/GPU-dependent, adding a hardware/driver reproducibility surface.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock/pixi.lock or a container digest for a declared platform (incl. CUDA version), and record the exact OpenMM patch release used.

gaps.missing: No deposited data accession (no GEO/SRA/ENA/Zenodo/figshare). Initial coordinate/parameter inputs (coords/*.rst, *.cnd; sigma_vdW/epsilon_vdW 'supplied in the input') are present in the GitHub repo but not versioned or documented as a dataset. The mitotic Hi-C map used for validation (second-diagonal target ~9.7 Mb) is referenced via citation [4], not re-deposited.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit input configurations + the reference Hi-C contact matrix (or a fetch script with accession) in a versioned archive (e.g., Zenodo snapshot) with a manifest mapping inputs to each of the 55 conformations.

gaps.missing: Repo contains only the simulator (Simulator_Chromatin.py) and parameter/init script (Pars.py). Code that converts simulation output (PDB/RST snapshots, per-force-group energies) into simulated Hi-C contact maps, rod-dimension measurements, and helicity/scaffold readouts is not evident in the repo prose/tree.
gaps.how_to_close: Add the contact-map computation, structural-metric, and figure scripts (with the parameters used) to the repository.

gaps.missing: github.com/norouzis/Super-loop-extrusion has no license and no tagged release/DOI; the paper links a floating repo HEAD (last push 2025-05-05) rather than a citable commit/archive snapshot.
gaps.how_to_close: Add an OSI license and mint a Zenodo/tagged release; cite the specific commit or archive DOI in the paper.
